claims.assertion: The trip was on RydeTAXI (metered, per-km rate $1.41 from F4/F6), so detour kilometres feed directly into the fare; the driver drove 24.2 km against an optimal 21.8 km, +2.4 km (+11%).

One off-route segment is registered on the GPS track (18:53–19:01: 3.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, adding 2.11 km, up to 995 m off the optimal route); no chat/stop request from the rider exists to explain it — there were no in-app messages at all.

The driver's only justification is 'a breakdown on the route … I took another way' (F8); RD-4 requires LTA traffic facts covering the substituted part of the optimal route before a reroute is exempt, so the burden is on that evidence, not on the driver's statement.

The LTA feed shows a vehicle breakdown reported 18:27 located 0 m from the optimal route on East Coast Parkway (left lane blocked), reported before the off-route segment began at 18:53 and within the trip window 18:35–19:23; the alternative-route alternative was not the one traversed but the one substituted by the driver.

The speed-band records (East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard both band 4, 30–39 km/h) do not meet RD-4(b)'s band 1/2 congestion test and in any event cannot exempt a segment on their own, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

The detour produced a billed excess of $3.33 (2.4 km × $1.41/km), of which the unexempt off-route segment's 2.11 km at the same trip rate is $2.98 to be refunded; the refund is the mileage component only, rounding to the cent.
Since the case is filed within 30 days of the trip, if the exemption fails the remedy is a refund, issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7, on the RydeTAXI terms that meter the trip.
Neither party's profile shows a prior upheld dispute (rider 0/1, driver 0/2 in 90 days), so no additional account flag is justified here; the case turns solely on the single off-route segment.

weaknesses: The driver has an LTA incident on record (F11, vehicle breakdown 18:27, 0 m from the optimal route, left lane blocked on East Coast Parkway) reported before the 18:53 off-route segment — RD-4(a) is the single strongest point against us and could exempt the segment entirely.

The total trip time was 48.6 min vs 28 min estimated (F2), which supports the driver's claim of slow conditions; only F9/F10 band-4 speeds (30–39 km/h) contradict that, and band 4 is not 'severe congestion' under RD-4(b).

Our only evidence that the rider never agreed to a reroute is the absence of chat (F7); if the rider had agreed verbally in the car, RD-5 cannot be tested and the driver's 'reasonable cause' story stands.

The 2.4 km total excess (F1) exceeds the single registered segment's 2.11 km (F3); the 0.29 km difference is map-matching residual that RD-2 does not refund, so our refund ceiling is less than the full billed $3.33 (F4).

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.98 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip: the fare is built from distance units, so detour kilometres feed directly into what the rider paid. The system record shows one registered off-route segment, 18:53–19:01, 3.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, +2.11 km, reaching up to 995 m off the optimal route [F3], which triggers the RD-1 duty to take the shortest and most direct route absent a reasonable cause. The billed fare breakdown confirms the meter (distance $34.08 on 24.2 km, no waiting, platform $1.47, no surge) [F5][F6], so any unexempt detour km map straight onto the rider's charge under RD-2.

The only defence available to the driver is the RD-4(a) reasonable-cause exemption, since there is no in-app chat at all [F7][F8], which removes any RD-3 rider-requested stop or RD-5 pre-departure agreed reroute. RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident on the substituted stretch of the optimal route, reported before the detour began and still listed within the trip window. claims.assertion: The trip was on RydeTAXI (metered, per-km rate $1.41 from F4/F6), so detour kilometres feed directly into the fare; the driver drove 24.2 km against an optimal 21.8 km, +2.4 km (+11%).

One off-route segment is registered on the GPS track (18:53–19:01: 3.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, adding 2.11 km, up to 995 m off the optimal route); no chat/stop request from the rider exists to explain it — there were no in-app messages at all.

The driver's only justification is 'a breakdown on the route … I took another way' (F8); RD-4 requires LTA traffic facts covering the substituted part of the optimal route before a reroute is exempt, so the burden is on that evidence, not on the driver's statement.

The LTA feed shows a vehicle breakdown reported 18:27 located 0 m from the optimal route on East Coast Parkway (left lane blocked), reported before the off-route segment began at 18:53 and within the trip window 18:35–19:23; the alternative-route alternative was not the one traversed but the one substituted by the driver.

The speed-band records (East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard both band 4, 30–39 km/h) do not meet RD-4(b)'s band 1/2 congestion test and in any event cannot exempt a segment on their own, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

The detour produced a billed excess of $3.33 (2.4 km × $1.41/km), of which the unexempt off-route segment's 2.11 km at the same trip rate is $2.98 to be refunded; the refund is the mileage component only, rounding to the cent.
Since the case is filed within 30 days of the trip, if the exemption fails the remedy is a refund, issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7, on the RydeTAXI terms that meter the trip.
Neither party's profile shows a prior upheld dispute (rider 0/1, driver 0/2 in 90 days), so no additional account flag is justified here; the case turns solely on the single off-route segment.

weaknesses: The driver has an LTA incident on record (F11, vehicle breakdown 18:27, 0 m from the optimal route, left lane blocked on East Coast Parkway) reported before the 18:53 off-route segment — RD-4(a) is the single strongest point against us and could exempt the segment entirely.

The total trip time was 48.6 min vs 28 min estimated (F2), which supports the driver's claim of slow conditions; only F9/F10 band-4 speeds (30–39 km/h) contradict that, and band 4 is not 'severe congestion' under RD-4(b).

Our only evidence that the rider never agreed to a reroute is the absence of chat (F7); if the rider had agreed verbally in the car, RD-5 cannot be tested and the driver's 'reasonable cause' story stands.

The 2.4 km total excess (F1) exceeds the single registered segment's 2.11 km (F3); the 0.29 km difference is map-matching residual that RD-2 does not refund, so our refund ceiling is less than the full billed $3.33 (F4).

claims.assertion: The single off-route segment is fully justified by a documented LTA incident: a vehicle breakdown with the left lane blocked was reported at 18:27 at 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. on the replaced portion of the optimal route (ECP), and the segment began at 18:53, after the report.

claims.assertion: The traffic record corroborates that the ECP was still degraded at the time of the trip: speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway during 18:24–19:28, covering the 18:53–19:01 segment window, and conditions were fair with 0.0 mm rain, so no weather explanation is in play.

Because the only off-route segment is exempt under RD-4(a), there is no unexempted deviation segment, so the RD-2 refund formula yields 0 and the correct outcome is no_action, with the RD-1 shortest-route obligation recorded as not breached.

The total ride is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90, distance $34.08, time $12.63, platform $1.47, no surge at 1.0x), so the rider's demand is limited to refunding the distance units attributable to unexempted detour km — of which there are none — and the billed excess of $3.33 (2.4 km x $1.41/km) maps onto the exempt segment.

No app-based stop, reroute or fee escalation occurred: there is no in-app chat and the driver's account shows no upheld dispute in 90 days, so nothing supports a FARE-1 style add-on refund and no RD-6 flag_account is triggered for my client.
Waiting fee charged was $0.00 and no extra undisclosed item appears in the fare breakdown, so no supplementary refund item exists beyond the disputed mileage.

weaknesses: The rider never agreed to the reroute: there is no in-app chat at all (F7), so the driver cannot claim passenger consent under RD-3 or RD-5 — the only defence is the RD-4(a) reasonable-cause exemption.

The off-route segment is long and far off: 3.98 km driven vs 1.87 km optimal, +2.11 km, reaching up to 995 m from the optimal route (F3), which the rider will argue is more than necessary for a lane-blocking breakdown on the ECP.

Trip duration 48.6 min vs 28 min estimate (F2) and the alternative route still shows only band 4, not band 1–2 (F9), which the rider may use to argue the reroute did not actually save time and was therefore not 'reasonable'.

points.response: Band 4 (30–39 km/h, F9/F10) is nowhere near RD-4(b)'s congestion test of band 1 or 2 (0–19 km/h), and RD-4(b) says a band record alone cannot exempt a segment anyway; D2 therefore corroborates slowdown at most, which is not the 'reasonable cause' RD-4(a) requires.

D3 assumes the very thing in dispute: RD-4(a) needs the incident to justify the substituted part of the optimal route, and the registered segment drove 3.98 km where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, reaching 995 m off-route (F3) — disproportionate to a single-point left-lane blockage (F11) — so RD-2 does not yield 0.

Conceded in part: the refund is mileage-only, but it is computed per unexempted segment (F3) at the trip's own $1.41/km rate (F4), which on 2.11 km is $2.98 — neither the full billed $3.33 nor zero, so RD-2 produces a positive amount.

We do not rely on FARE-1 add-ons and we do not seek an RD-6 flag; but D5's own premise — no chat at all (F7) — defeats any RD-3/RD-5 consent defence, and the driver's written statement (F8) cannot override the GPS record of a 2.11 km detour (F3).
Agreed that no waiting fee or undisclosed add-on is in play ($0.00 waiting, platform $1.47, F6); the whole dispute is the metered distance, whose refundable part is still $2.98 under RD-2.

Withdrawn: I no longer assert the LTA breakdown record is inapplicable — on the record it is the strongest driver-side point, and the rider's case now rests on the detour (2.11 km, 995 m off-route, F3) being disproportionate to a single-point lane blockage (F11) reported 26 minutes before the segment began.

Correct and not contested: a RydeTAXI meter means detour km enter the fare (F4, F6), so the case turns entirely on whether the single registered off-route segment is exempt — but RD-1 is not violated where a reasonable cause exists, so the +2.4 km figure alone proves nothing.

The absence of in-app chat (F7) removes RD-3/RD-5 consent, which we have never claimed; it does not touch the RD-4(a) reasonable-cause exemption, which the driver asserted in his statement (F8) and which the LTA feed proves.
